svg.text: Keyword families: how much is checked, and how well
2,893 language-by-family rules are defined. 91 are measured against a parser (7 languages), 721 more only by a decoy test, 2,081 not tested yet.
Measured against a parser: the lower of recall and precision, in %
R = the family misses constructs the parser sees; P = it fires where the parser sees none. † corpus not pinned (exploratory).
Dashed grey italic: under 10 functions. · not tested yet. – tested, the construct never occurs. Rows worst first. Draft = the contract is a draft.
Each family keyword planted in a comment and in a string
Comments are stripped before any family is counted, as designed.
Strings are not: a keyword inside a string counts like code. That is
documented behaviour (issue #2535), but it conflicts with the families'
written contracts, so it is a decision for the maintainers, not a fix.
One repository per language; the parser's reading is our interpretation
of each family's contract, not ground truth. Cells are measurements on
one corpus, not proof a family is right everywhere.
